page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7a.16xlarge is a high-density compute-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture using KVM virtualization. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7T83 processor operating at a base clock frequency of 2.55 GHz. The hardware layout comprises 32 physical cores and 64 dedicated virtual CPUs via simultaneous multithreading, supported by 128 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 RAM-to-vCPU allocation ratio. Baseline network connectivity reaches 16 Gbps. This instance configuration does not include local NVMe storage drives or integrated GPU accelerators.

In benchmark evaluations, the server exhibits high multi-core execution capabilities, placing in the top quartile for stress-ng CPU tests, PassMark CPU benchmarks, and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression. Specialized instruction processing is strong across cryptographic, ray tracing, and image processing tests. Key-value datastore testing demonstrates robust throughput with Redis SET operations achieving 61.81 million operations per second. However, single-threaded execution metrics—including single-threaded gzip compression and Geekbench single-core scores—fall within the average performance bracket, as do uncached large-block memory bandwidth reads and writes.

The 1:2 memory-to-core ratio offers efficient compute density for tasks that demand high parallel CPU capacity without requiring large memory footprints. This hardware trade-off minimizes idle RAM costs while maximizing CPU core availability. Because local storage is absent, persistent data must be backed by remote block storage, introducing network dependency for I/O operations. The ecs.c7a.16xlarge is well suited for compute-intensive workloads, parallel batch processing, continuous integration build servers, software compilation using Clang, static web serving backends, and distributed in-memory caching layers.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7a.16xlarge is a compute-optimized cloud instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7T83 processor running at 2.55 GHz across 32 physical cores and 64 dedicated vCPUs. Configured with 128 GB of RAM (2.0 GB per core) and a 16 Gbps baseline network interface, this instance omits local disk storage and GPU hardware, relying on network-attached block storage for persistent data. Benchmark results highlight top-tier multi-core execution in stress-ng and PassMark CPU evaluations, alongside strong performance in cryptography, image processing, and Redis key-value operations reaching 61.81 million SET operations per second. While uncached memory throughput and single-threaded gzip compression rank in the average tier, the 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM balance maximizes compute resource density. This profile provides high cost efficiency for CPU-bound microservices, software compilation, CI/CD pipelines, parallelized data processing, and in-memory caching workloads.
